To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the capacity to synthesize fatty acids from glucose in adipose tissue was reduced in early weaned goats and that the reduction in lipogenic capacity was due primarily to a reduction in the activity of LPL.
the activities of lipogenic enzyme in the omental adipose tissues of goat kids were affected differently after weaning.
the lipoprotein lipolysis and lipogenesis of goat adipose tissue were closely related to the intake of metabolizable energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of weaning on the lipogenic capacity of goat kids.
the effects of age and weaning on the activities of enzymes involved in the lipogenic process in adipose tissue of young growing goats.
the regulation of lipogenic capacity in adipose tissue of growing goats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the changes in lipogenic enzyme activity in goat adipose tissue and the changes in plasma glucose and non-esterified fatty acids after weaning were related to the restoration of lipid reserves.
the lipogenic capacity of adipose tissue is more sensitive to weaning than that of liver.
the weaning process in young goats is characterized by a marked reduction in lipogenic capacity of adipose tissue, but not of liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lipogenic enzymes of adipose tissue are sensitive to changes in energy intake.
weaning is a major stressor for young goats.
the lipogenic capacity of adipose tissue of goat kids was reduced immediately after weaning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LPL is a key enzyme for lipogenesis after weaning and its activity is closely related to the metabolizable energy intake of goats.
the lipogenic capacity of adipose tissue and the lipolytic capacity of adipose and liver are closely related to the availability of energy and glucose.
LPL activity is a key determinant of adipose tissue lipogenesis.
